name: Zealand – Academy of Technologies and Business
about: Zealand is a business academy (erhvervsakademi) with several campuses on Zealand. It offers two fully English-taught first degrees, both three-and-a-half-year professional bachelor degrees on its Næstved campus: Architectural Technology and Construction Management, and Cybersecurity. Both include a one-semester internship.

languageOfInstruction.note: Zealand lists two full-degree programmes in English. Both also run in Danish.

sources.title: Zealand's admission page for its English-taught degrees gives the same subject requirements. For ATCM, English B or an accepted test (IELTS Academic 6.5 and others). It ranks applicants on grade average, other education, work, time abroad and higher subject levels, and sometimes interviews. Non-EU applicants pay a EUR 300 application fee.
sources.quote: Please note that the English requirements cannot be replaced by an English test, as English B is a specific requirement for admission to the program, whether it is the Danish- or English-taught version. [...] The requirements for Architectural Technology and Construction Management are as follows: English B or equivalent level of English. [...] IELTS (Academic) with a minimum average score of 6.5 [...] Evaluation criteria [...] Average grade from your qualifying exam Other relevant higher education Relevant work experience of minimum 3 months part time Studies abroad, volunteering, military service etc. for a minimum of 3 months Specific requirements passed on a higher level than required In certain cases we do an admission interview [...] The application fee is a one-time payment of 300 EUR.

sources.title: Zealand identifies itself as an Academy of Technologies and Business.

notes: For IB applicants, Zealand still asks for "Mathematical Studies, standard level (SL)", a course the IB replaced from 2019. This site treats Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation or Analysis and Approaches, at SL or HL, as meeting it; Zealand does not say so, so confirm with Zealand.
Non-EU applicants without a Danish residence permit that gives free tuition pay a one-time application fee of EUR 300 by 15 March. It is deducted from the first year's tuition if they accept a place.
The admission pages put Zealand's contact address in Køge. Both English-taught programmes are taught in Næstved.

programmes.about: Construction management: planning, coordinating and delivering building projects from housing to multi-storey and renovation work, with BIM and a 20-week internship. selection.description: Applicants are ranked on the grade average of their qualifying exam, other relevant higher education, at least three months of relevant work, at least three months of study abroad, volunteering or military service, and required subjects passed at a higher level than required.

requirements.label: An IB Diploma, or DP Course Results with at least 18 points, grade 3 in all six subjects and three of them at HL

officialWording.text: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2.

requirements.note: The rule is national, not this institution's. The Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with grade 3 or more in all six subjects and three at HL, like a two-year hf without overbygning, which gives access to erhvervsakademi and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2. This is a professionsbachelor programme, which the Agency names directly. The institution's own page names the IB but says nothing about Course Results, so a Course candidate should confirm with admissions in writing. The award does not waive the subject requirements below.

sources.title: DP Course Results (formerly the IB Certificate) of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three subjects at HL, are a qualifying examination in Denmark on the same terms as a two-year hf without overbygning: they give access to erhvervsakademi- and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2, and to a university bachelor only after two successive raises of upper-secondary subject level, at least one to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag. Course Results under 18 points, or containing any subject at grade 1 or 2, are not a qualifying examination at all. A full IB Diploma of 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark.
sources.quote: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2. Ansøgere med et Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results på mindst 18 point og mindst karakteren 3 i alle fag kan derudover få adgang til en universitetsbacheloruddannelse gennem kvote 1 og 2 ved enten at supplere med enkeltfag efter samme regler som hf’erne eller tage deres IB-eksamen om for at få et IB Diploma – Retake.

requirements.note: The source asks IB applicants for "Mathematical Studies, standard level (SL)". sources.title: DP Course Results (formerly the IB Certificate) of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three subjects at HL, are a qualifying examination in Denmark on the same terms as a two-year hf without overbygning: they give access to erhvervsakademi- and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2, and to a university bachelor only after two successive raises of upper-secondary subject level, at least one to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag. Course Results under 18 points, or containing any subject at grade 1 or 2, are not a qualifying examination at all. A full IB Diploma of 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark.
sources.quote: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2. Ansøgere med et Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results på mindst 18 point og mindst karakteren 3 i alle fag kan derudover få adgang til en universitetsbacheloruddannelse gennem kvote 1 og 2 ved enten at supplere med enkeltfag efter samme regler som hf’erne eller tage deres IB-eksamen om for at få et IB Diploma – Retake.
